name: Harpak-Ulma Packaging, LLC
old_description: From concept to consumer, we provide end-to-end Weighing, Distribution, and Packaging Solutions that minimize waste, maximize efficiency and drive innovation.
about:
Harpak-ULMA Packaging, LLC is headquartered in Taunton, Massachusetts. The business traces its roots to 1994 when the Harlfinger family, drawing on over 30 years of packaging experience, established Harpak. On July 19, 2010, Harpak merged with ULMA Packaging—a company with more than 50 years of equipment and systems expertise—to form the current entity. The combined organization maintains a family-business atmosphere and emphasizes long-term customer relationships.

The company supplies end-to-end weighing, distribution, and packaging solutions, including vertical form-fill-seal (VFFS) machines, tray sealers, thermoformers, vision inspection systems, and metal detection/rejection equipment. It also provides installation, factory acceptance testing (including remote FAT), operator and maintenance training through its AICET-accredited academy, preventive maintenance programs, and a 24/7/365 parts and technical support network staffed by PMMI-certified technicians. Harpak-ULMA operates across North America with a field service presence and holds an NPS of 84 percent.

Primary markets include food processing (bakery, poultry, cheese, snack, and case-ready packaging), medical device packaging, and industrial packaging. The firm works with corporations in those sectors and, since 2024, supports Cabinplant weighing and packaging equipment owners in the U.S. and Canada through a full partnership.

Harpak-ULMA cites its six core values—integrity, commitment, service, excellence, teamwork, and innovation—as the foundation of its differentiation. The merger combined ULMA’s advanced design and manufacturing technologies with Harpak’s cultivated customer relationships, aiming to deliver a wider range of fully integrated packaging solutions while preserving a personal, family-business approach.

name: Harpeth River Woodworks
old_description: We create each of our high quality projects with passion and craftsmanship, tailored to elevate your space.
about:
Harpeth River Woodworks operates from Nolensville, Tennessee, with a fabrication shop in nearby Chapel Hill. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, but it presents itself as a woodworking studio dedicated to heirloom-quality furniture and cabinetry.

The shop produces custom cabinetry for kitchens, baths, and built-ins, as well as one-of-a-kind furniture pieces shipped nationwide. It also offers CNC machining services including custom signs, engraving, CNC doors, and custom part machining. A design phase using 3D renderings precedes production, and flat-pack packages are available for DIY enthusiasts and contractors. The facility blends traditional hand tools with modern CNC equipment, though specific machine models and headcount are not published.

Customers range from homeowners seeking lasting pieces to contractors and businesses needing custom millwork. The company notes that its furniture graces homes across the country and that it serves both residential and commercial projects.

Harpeth River Woodworks emphasizes that its work is built to outlast the trees it comes from, using real wood, traditional joinery, and durable finishes. The collaborative process—listen, design, create—is described as the core differentiator, with the goal of delivering pieces that can be passed down for generations.

name: Hart Electric
old_description: Hart Electric specializes in off-road and custom applications such as mining, agriculture and industrial. .
about:
Hart Electric has operated from Lostant, Illinois since 1984. The company was founded that year and has since focused on wire harness and cable assembly for off-road and custom applications.

The shop builds wire harnesses and cables to customer specifications, offering a suite of value-added processes: computer-aided continuity testing, sonic splicing with an advanced sonic welder, custom thermal-transfer marking on heat-shrink tubing (0.25″ to 4″ lengths, 1/16″ to 2″ sizes), hot tin dipping for copper and copper alloys, nylon braiding (24 to 36 strands), and hot stamping for wire sizes from 8 AWG to 18 AWG. The company emphasizes fast quoting and quick turnaround for time-sensitive orders.

Hart Electric serves mining, agriculture, industrial, and other off-road equipment sectors. Customers include manufacturers of custom off-road machinery who require harnesses built to exacting specifications and delivered within tight schedules.

The company's stated promise is that “your project will become our project; your sense of urgency becomes ours,” backed by a management team available to address concerns. Plant manager John Hartenbower oversees operations, and the firm highlights its commitment to quality craftsmanship and incorporating the latest assembly technologies.

name: Harvest Bakery Service Inc
old_description: Suppling all major brands of equipment to the baking industry!
about:
Harvest Equipment and Fabrication Inc began in 1999 when Tim Kemp and Jeff Giesel founded the company in Burnsville, Minnesota. The business started as a provider of bakery equipment service, sales, parts, and consultation for the Midwestern market.

Today the company supplies new and used bakery machinery from major brands, covering categories such as mixers, ovens, dividers, sheeters, slicers, and packaging equipment. It also operates a fabrication shop that retrofits and modernizes older equipment, and offers consulting services including plant planning, installation coordination, process design, and employee training. The facility in Lakeville, Minnesota, sits 15 minutes from the MSP airport and serves as a showroom where customers can view and test equipment.

Harvest serves retail and industrial bakeries, food manufacturers, and commercial processing operations across the Midwest and globally. Its technicians have performed installations and repairs worldwide, and the company brokers used equipment for clients ranging from single machines to complete production lines.

The founders recognized that increasing lead times and labor shortages create demand for custom solutions, so Harvest focuses on retrofitting existing machinery and integrating automation to extend equipment life and improve throughput.

name: Harvest Food Products Co Inc
old_description: Family-founded and family-led, Harvest Food Products has spent more than 40 years creating authentic, high-quality foods that inspire menus and delight customers everywhere.
about:
Harvest Food Products was founded in 1982 in San Francisco by Chinese immigrants Chau and Khai Kha, who began manufacturing Asian foods such as potstickers, spring rolls, and wontons from their storefront. The family-owned business secured USDA approval and later moved to a 40,000-square-foot USDA-inspected facility in Hayward, California. Today, the company is led by the founders’ children Danny, Connie, and Peter Kha and operates three USDA-inspected facilities in Hayward.

The company produces a wide range of frozen foods including dumplings, bao, egg rolls, battered proteins, and meal kits for retail, foodservice, and private-label channels. Its capabilities cover co-packing, private-label manufacturing, custom formulation, recipe scaling, small-batch testing, and R&D. Production sites feature advanced fryers, steamers, and freezers, supporting large-scale production for customers across the United States and internationally.

Harvest serves grocery and club retailers, restaurants and catering operations, institutional and foodservice kitchens, as well as startups and established brands seeking co-packing or private-label partnerships. Its product portfolio addresses diverse dietary needs with certified gluten-free and halal options, alongside traditional Asian specialties.

The company emphasizes authentic family recipes, fresh ingredients, and convenient preparation as its founding principles. It maintains BRC Global Standards, GFSI, and USDA certifications, plus gluten-free and halal verifications, to ensure quality and inclusivity. An in-house R&D team collaborates with partners from concept to production, focusing on flavor development and packaging optimization.

name: Hawaii Medical Research Center
old_description: ¨への社会的な関心が高まるとともに、医療技術の進歩が著しく、医療にかかわるè€
about:
Hawaii Medical Research Center operates a cadaver laboratory in Honolulu, Hawaii, established to provide a dedicated venue for medical education, research, and surgical skill development. The facility was created in response to growing societal concern for medical safety and rapid advances in medical technology, which have increased demand for hands-on training that cannot be conducted on living patients.

The center provides a fully equipped cadaver lab where physicians, dentists, and other healthcare professionals can practice advanced surgical techniques, test new medical devices, and conduct anatomical research. Cadavers are sourced through the American Association of Tissue Banks, with each donor screened for infectious disease and accompanied by safety documentation. The facility operates under Hawaii state licensure and follows the Uniform Anatomical Gift Act (1968), which governs anatomical donation in the United States.

Primary users include orthopedic surgeons, neurosurgeons, plastic surgeons, dental specialists, and medical researchers from Japan and other countries. The center has supported research projects funded by Japan's Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research (Kakenhi) and has exhibited at major Japanese medical society meetings, including the Japanese Orthopaedic Association, Japan Neurosurgical Society, and Japanese Society of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery. It also collaborates with Kauai Search & Rescue, providing cadavers for K-9 search dog training.

The center was founded to address the lack of accessible cadaver-based training environments in Japan, where legal restrictions limit anatomical dissection to specific university settings. By operating in Hawaii under U.S. law, it offers a legally compliant alternative for international medical professionals seeking realistic surgical practice and device validation.
